messages:
maria: quick idea — building on our deploy bot threads: propose adding a small set of flags and a tiny templating flow so engineers don't do the same manual steps during change windows. rough flags: `--hold-until <RFC3339>`, `--pin=service:version`, `--canary-pct N`, `--auto-rollback={off|5xx>pct|latency>ms}`, and `--release-notes /path/to/template.md`. wanted to surface this early for feedback.

sam: +1 to `--hold-until`. we should wire it into the calendar guard so the bot refuses deploys outside windows unless `--force` + an approval. also: show the hold-until in the preflight summary UI.

maria: yeah — thinking preflight shows: pinned versions, hold window, canary pct, auto-rollback policy. short CLI example:
```bash
/deploy --service payments --pin=payments:v2.1.3 --canary-pct 10 --hold-until 2026-04-01T10:00:00Z --release-notes ./rn.md
```

jess: would prefer a `pinset` subcommand so you can commit a group of pins and reuse them across deploys. e.g. `deploy pinset create nightly-backfill --pins payments:v2.1.3,search:v4.0` then `--pinset nightly-backfill`. less typing, less human error.

sam: pinset is nice. also add `--dry-run=preflight` that outputs the exact plan the bot will execute (routes, versions, evaluated kernels) so SRE can eyeball before release.

ops-bot: ticket created infra#4321: "deploy-bot: scheduler flags + pinset + release-notes template" (assigned to @maria).

maria: thx ops-bot. random thought on `--auto-rollback`: default off. config should accept a small policy object: fail_rate_pct, window_secs, min_rps, and an allowlist for safety. sample YAML we'd store as a policy: 
```yaml
auto_rollback:
  enabled: true
  fail_rate_pct: 5
  window_secs: 300
  min_rps: 50
  grace_period_secs: 120
```

troy: big +1 to hysteresis. also we should require a canary baseline measurement before enabling auto-rollback (so a bad baseline doesn't trigger immediate rollback). we need a short circuit: `--auto-rollback=force` only for emergencies and gated by 2 approvers.

kia: on release notes — propose a small template engine that inserts the deploy metadata automatically: pins, canary %, change window, owner, rollback plan. example template snippet: 
```md
Summary: {{summary}}
Components: {{pins}}
Risk: {{risk}}
Rollback plan: {{rollback_plan}}
Preflight: {{preflight_url}}
```
Then `--release-notes` can take either a path or `auto` to generate a PR body we can attach to the release ticket.

jess: auditability: please log the pinset id + user + commit hash in the deploy event so rollbacks can quickly map to exact code. also surface the pinset diff in the preflight UI.

maria: agreed. for rollout UX: preflight card shows: pinset (if any), changed routes, canary pct, hold-until, auto-rollback policy, and quick buttons: Approve / Pause / Abort. clicking Approve triggers the bot with a pinned comment and records approvers.

sam: implementation scope: small PoC — CLI flags, pinset persistence (DB table), preflight renderer + templating hook. console buttons and calendar integration as follow-ups. estimate 3 devs for 2 sprints.

maria: i'll draft a short RFC with command grammar, sample templates, and the DB schema. pinging @eng-releases for any strong objections before i kick off. timeline: PoC by EOW sprint (aiming to demo in shiproom). :rocket:

jess: sounds good. happy to help with schema and preflight UI bits.

troy: +1. i'll write the auto-rollback unit tests once the policy shape is final.

kia: adding a small checklist for release-notes auto-gen: ensure PR body sanitization, escapes for markdown, and link to preflight artifacts.

sam: leaving a couple of micro UX asks in the RFC: show pinned versions inline in the timeline, and add a small `why-pinned` annotation.

maria: thanks all — i'll post the RFC link here when ready. adding this to the sprint board and tagging infra#4321.

jess: :+1:

sam: lgtm

ops-bot: note: infra#4321 moved to "in progress" by maria.
